production_change.summary: Added a complementary 'Alpha-Specific Positive Requirement' gate to the existing Step-7A negative invalidation veto. A matched A001 result must now clear BOTH: (A) no decisive invalidation/opposition semantics (Step-7A veto, unchanged), AND (B) affirmative directional easing semantics (new Step-7A.2 gate). Applied at the single production path capable of emitting a final matched_alpha under Pure-LLM Alpha semantic authority (map_claim_to_alpha, immediately after the Step-7A veto, before evidence-stance attachment) -- traced and confirmed there is no other path (deterministic scoring is diagnostic-only and never assigns the final matched_alpha; the LLM 'none'/'unavailable' outcomes never risk a positive A001 result in the first place).
production_change.why_two_files: claim_semantics.py: new classify_a001_directional_semantics()/ALPHA_POSITIVE_REQUIREMENT_CLASSIFIERS/alpha_positive_requirement_satisfied() -- the semantic classification logic itself, alongside the existing alpha_specific_invalidation_matched() this complements. alpha_mapper.py: the single call site wiring the new gate into map_claim_to_alpha's final matched_alpha resolution, mirroring exactly how the Step-7A veto is wired in. Both files were necessary for the same reason Step 7A needed both.

positive_requirement_semantics.not_a_literal_five_string_gate: Each class is a tuple of regex patterns covering real semantic variants (explicit cuts, 'cutting rates', 'rate-cut cycle', 'easing cycle', 'monetary/policy easing', 'fed is cutting/easing', 'falling/declining/lower rates', 'borrowing costs falling', 'central bank shifting to easier policy', 'rate decline', plus confident affirmative-expectation phrasing -- 'markets expect/anticipate/are pricing in cuts', 'fed is set to/poised to/expected to cut') -- not merely the five taxonomy anchor phrases quoted in the Step-7A.1 recommendation.
positive_requirement_semantics.mention_only_excluded: A dedicated mention-only check ('focused on whether', 'debate/question/uncertainty...whether', 'whether the fed will') resolves to CONDITIONAL_OR_UNCERTAIN before the positive patterns are even checked, so a bare 'cut rates' inside a 'will the Fed cut?' framing never counts.
positive_requirement_semantics.modality_handling: A direct-positive pattern match still carrying a conditional/modal marker (if/unless/could/may/might/would/potentially -- reusing the existing _CONDITIONAL_PATTERN) downgrades to CONDITIONAL_OR_UNCERTAIN. Confident affirmative-expectation phrasing (its own separate pattern group) is exempt from this downgrade, since it already encodes non-hedged certainty in its own wording.

boundary_preservation.A001_vs_A003: Liquidity-only evidence (no falling-rate/easing semantics) classifies GENERIC_RATE_CONTEXT or NO_RATE_SEMANTICS for A001 and is unaffected for A003 (gate is A001-only).
boundary_preservation.A001_vs_A501: Recession-risk evidence alone does not imply A001; classifies NO_RATE_SEMANTICS or GENERIC_RATE_CONTEXT, never POSITIVE_EASING merely from a possible future policy response.
boundary_preservation.A001_vs_A304: Rate-sensitive valuation pressure ('high yields pressure technology valuations') classifies GENERIC_RATE_CONTEXT for A001 and is unaffected for A304 (gate is A001-only).

positive_requirement_semantics.registry_extensibility: ALPHA_POSITIVE_REQUIREMENT_CLASSIFIERS is table-driven and currently registers only A001; a no-op (always satisfied) for every other Alpha, per explicit instruction not to build a ten-Alpha framework now.

tests.step7a_test_updated_reason: test_boundary_recession_evidence_does_not_become_a001_even_if_llm_selected_it renamed to test_boundary_recession_evidence_negative_veto_does_not_overreach and its assertion updated: the Step-7A NEGATIVE veto still correctly does not fire for this claim (documented, unchanged behavior), but the claim is now correctly rejected end-to-end by the separate Step-7A.2 POSITIVE-requirement gate instead, since it contains no affirmative easing evidence. Not a weakening of the original test's intent -- the negative-veto-scope assertion is preserved and still checked explicitly.

offline_replay.note: No target N was set in advance and none was optimized for. The semantic gate (not a numeric target) is the authority; it happens to reject all 66 original claims and all 29 residual claims because none of them, on independent inspection, expresses affirmative directional easing -- consistent with the Step-7A.1 audit's own independent finding of 0/29 valid positive support.

ready_reason: No survivors remain in either the full 66-claim or 29-claim residual replay; the rejection is not a bare count outcome but a semantic one -- inspection confirms every original opposition/hawkish, generic-rate, mention-only, and conditional-cut claim correctly resolves to a non-POSITIVE_EASING class. Positive A001 recall is independently confirmed intact via 5 positive controls (including 2 that avoid the literal phrase 'rate cut' entirely). A001/A003, A001/A501, and A001/A304 boundaries all pass. No new regression was found in 56 focused + 508 relevant-subsystem tests; broader full-suite results are recorded separately below.

test_results_step7a2_full_suite.new_error_root_cause: ONE single root cause across all 39 new errors, individually verified across 4 different test files (test_exact_semantic_replay.py, test_replay_behavioral_equivalence.py, test_replay_modes.py, test_replay_provider_zero.py) in addition to the two files shown in the summary, all failing at the SAME line: tests/replay/conftest.py:221's shared `eligible_live_source` fixture asserts `model.calls == 4` on its `OfflineSemanticModel` mock. That mock's alpha_classifier branch always returns `payload['alpha_taxonomy'][0]['alpha_id']` -- 'the taxonomy's own first alpha_id, sorted' per its own docstring -- which is A001 (alphabetically/numerically first among the 10 canonical Alpha IDs), REGARDLESS of the fixture's fixed claim text ('AI demand drives GPU demand and revenue growth while valuation risk creates downside' -- pure NVDA/AI content, zero rate/cut/easing language). Before this task, that synthetic A001 selection passed through unchallenged (Step 7A's negative veto never fires on this text -- it doesn't invalidate A001's thesis, it's simply unrelated), so matched_alpha stayed non-null and B1's own LLM stance-upgrade pass legitimately fired a real 4th call. This task's new positive-requirement gate correctly classifies this claim NO_RATE_SEMANTICS for A001 and rejects the match, so matched_alpha becomes None, B1's stance upgrade has no Alpha to evaluate and never fires, and model.calls drops to 3, tripping the fixture's hardcoded '== 4' assertion for every one of the 39 tests that depend on this one shared fixture (directly or via a fixture chain).
test_results_step7a2_full_suite.new_error_is_production_regression_ratio: This is a test-infrastructure artifact, not a production defect: no real Provider/LLM would plausibly select A001 (Rate Cut Cycle) for 'AI demand drives GPU demand and revenue growth' content -- the mock's 'always pick the alphabetically-first taxonomy entry' convenience convention happens to coincide with A001 purely by alphabetical accident, and was never meant to assert anything about A001-specific semantics; these 39 tests exercise exact-replay atomicity, semantic-call binding, and corruption-handling mechanics using A001 only as an arbitrary non-null placeholder. This exact assertion has ALREADY been bumped once before (the fixture's own comment: '4, not the pre-Alpha-Authority-Migration 3') during a prior, similarly-authorized semantic-authority change -- confirming this is a known, precedented, expected-to-need-future-maintenance call-count tripwire, not a stable production invariant. None of this task's own 56 focused tests or the 508 relevant Alpha-Mapper/claim_semantics-dependent subsystem tests regressed.
test_results_step7a2_full_suite.new_error_remediation_not_implemented: Not fixed in this task (touching the widely-shared tests/replay/conftest.py fixture, used across 6+ test files for unrelated replay-binding/corruption/atomicity mechanics, is outside this task's explicit narrow-scope authorization -- 'prefer extending tests/test_qqq_a001_mapping_remediation.py,' 'do not touch unrelated modules'). Recommended narrow follow-up: update the shared fixture's fixed claim text to include genuine rate-cut/easing language (so the mock's canned A001 selection is semantically defensible) OR change the mock's placeholder-alpha-selection convention to avoid relying on alphabetical-sort-produces-A001 as an implicit, undocumented assumption -- then re-bump the call-count assertion as needed, exactly as was done once before.
